A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PDFBench. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and added supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, dataset-overlap analyses, mutation experiments, and comparisons of evaluation metrics in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-5.1 evaluations and measurements of metric computation times.

M1.justification: New Appendix G proposes staged evaluation: initially screen using cheaper metrics, then compute Foldability and IPR Recovery. The existing metric computations, Repeat algorithm, and protein-generation methods remain unchanged. This is a new recommended procedure, without evidence that it was used for the retained benchmark results.

E1.justification: Both versions use MolinstTest with 5,876 proteins and SwissTest with 1,057 proteins, retaining description-guided, GO-guided, IPR-guided, and joint-keyword tasks. The GPT-5.1 and timing experiments use existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds GPT-5.1 to the three keyword-guided comparisons in Tables 9–11, labeled GPT-5 or GPT5 in the tables and identified in Appendix F and Table 12. The original eight protein-design baselines retain their participation.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce prompted GPT-5.1 generation settings and a timing protocol using random samples of 50 and 500 SwissTest proteins, with specified metric selections and joint computations. Existing dataset processing and baseline evaluation settings remain unchanged; revised scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G and Table 13 add an analysis of computational costs across metrics and sample sizes. The earlier overlap, mutation-sensitivity, metric-correlation, and retrieval-strategy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports uncertainty for description-guided results but only point estimates for keyword-guided results. v3 systematically adds plus/minus uncertainty values across most metrics in keyword-guided Tables 9–11, substantially expanding statistical reporting. Both versions state three runs with different seeds; no increase in run count is reported.

E6.justification: Diversity results change substantially: ProDVa's description-guided sequence/structural diversity changes from 83.29/36.92 to 46.10/52.59 in Tables 2 and 8, while its GO-guided sequence diversity changes from 98.17 to 42.84 in Tables 3 and 11. These revisions alter rankings. v3 also adds GPT-5.1 results and computation times, and changes natural-protein retrieval accuracy in Table 2 from 88.65 to 89.01. The cause of the diversity revisions is not explained.

T1.justification: The task formulations and mathematical metric definitions in Appendix C are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds practical benchmarking guidance as a contribution, pointing to Appendix G. The central claims concerning a comprehensive function-guided benchmark, two settings, sixteen metrics, and analysis of metric relationships remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The limitations expand from small test-set size to heterogeneous training datasets and unavailable training resources, clarifying that comparisons concern released model weights rather than isolated architecture effects. New appendices interpret GPT-5.1's alignment versus foldability and discuss computational constraints. Takeaway V also shifts its wording from functional similarity to structural similarity.

D1.justification: Table 12 supplies GPT-5.1 prompts, temperature 1.0, and top_p 0.1. Appendix G specifies four RTX3090 GPUs and a 48-core CPU for timing measurements. The abstract gives an explicit code/data repository, replacing v2's project-page and anonymous-GitHub access descriptions; actual online availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 develops comparisons with RFDiffusion plus ProteinMPNN and other conditional-design workflows, and discusses Pinal's reported wet-lab validation as motivation. This extends the existing positioning without changing the benchmark's central novelty claim. Other reference changes largely update or complete already cited works.

P1.justification: v3 shortens metric takeaways, reorganizes Appendix A into subsections, adds impact and acknowledgement sections, and changes author order, affiliation text, and publication headers. Most main-text prose and the overall scientific narrative remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column main paper and reference section, substantially changing figure and table sizing, placement, and panel arrangement. Algorithm 1 moves to a separate page; Tables 12–13 are added and keyword tables become denser. Table 3's language-alignment headings are corrected to match the underlying metric ordering.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses missing keyword-task uncertainty reporting, corrects Table 3's metric headings, and adds useful comparator settings, timing evidence, and training-data limitations. These improve transparency and practical usability. However, the large diversity revisions remain unexplained, and v3 introduces an inconsistency: natural-protein IPR Recovery is 83.22/87.39 in Table 3 for IPR/joint guidance but remains 100 in Table 10. These issues limit the overall gain.
